findings.Quote: He didn't think about that.
findings.Note: Directly telling the reader he's not thinking about the memory, immediately after rendering it in detail, is a telling-not-showing contradiction in technique — the paragraph performs the opposite of its claim.
findings.Fix: Cut the line and let the juxtaposition of memory and roster-thoughts do the work, or replace with a concrete action that displaces the memory.

findings.Quote:
He'd been paid to move it once, sealed. He opened it.

Then he copied it, because at nineteen he'd learned one thing
findings.Fix: align ages — earlier in the same beat he is stated to be twenty when he copies the slug ('He was twenty, and he knew exactly what he was copying'), but this clause attributes the lesson behind the copying to being nineteen; make both instances consistent (e.g. 'because he'd learned at nineteen' as backstory framing, or change the first line to also say nineteen)

findings.Quote: That was four years gone, and it had made them into men who would not have recognized the kids they'd been.
findings.Note: Generic aphorism about change that tells rather than shows the transformation, undercutting the specificity built up in the rest of the paragraph.
findings.Fix: Cut the sentence or replace with a concrete detail unique to these two men.

findings.Quote: under him the floor seemed to shift — not really, but that was the feeling of it, the floor moving out from under him faster than he could plant his feet
findings.Note: The hedge-then-explain construction ('not really, but that was the feeling of it') tells the reader how to read the metaphor instead of trusting it, and the image itself is a stock vertigo cliché dressed up with qualifiers.
findings.Fix: Cut the hedge; either commit to the physical sensation directly or drop the image entirely.

findings.Quote: the only language they'd ever shared that had never needed words
findings.Note: Vague, tells the emotional weight rather than showing what the click actually conveys; reads as filler sentiment rather than concrete information.
findings.Fix: Cut the abstraction and specify what the click's rhythm/pattern actually signaled.

findings.Quote: It felt like safety. It kept feeling like safety right up until it turned into a door that only opened one way.
findings.Note: Aphoristic telling that generalizes Tavi's interiority into a stock 'safety is a trap' truism rather than showing it through specific detail.
findings.Fix: Cut the abstraction and ground it in one concrete memory of Tavi's own payment/debt.

findings.Quote: It was the worst thing Tavi had ever been handed in a room.
findings.Note: Vague intensifier that tells us the weight of the moment without showing what makes trust the worst burden; 'worst thing... in a room' is abstract and unearned given the beat's brevity.
findings.Fix: Specify the actual burden, e.g. 'Rafi's trust was heavier than any contract Tavi had signed.'

findings.Quote: Tavi knew it the way he knew the camera lag — flat and certain, a weight sitting in his chest.
findings.Note: Mixes a stated-fact simile (camera lag) with a vague bodily-weight cliché for emotion; the two halves don't cohere and the second half tells rather than shows.
findings.Fix: Cut the weight-in-chest clause or replace with a concrete physical detail.

findings.Quote: On the floor above him, at this same moment, Reza was thickening the north corridor.
findings.Note: States simultaneous action as fact from Tavi's POV without explaining how he could know this in real time, undercutting the 'flat and certain' knowledge claim that follows.
findings.Fix: Clarify this is inference from earlier observation, not present-tense perception.

findings.Quote: Tavi caught the wrist with his right hand, the graze-arm folding wrong under the weight
findings.Note: If Tavi caught the wrist with his right hand, it's unclear why the 'graze-arm' (presumably the injured arm) is the one folding under weight — the sentence conflates which arm is doing what action, creating ambiguity as to whether the right hand and the graze-arm are the same limb.
findings.Fix: Clarify which arm is injured and which is catching: e.g. 'Tavi caught the wrist with his good hand, his graze-arm buckling as he took the weight.'

findings.Quote: Tavi could read which way it would fall before Reza moved at all: Reza was going to let him through.
findings.Note: Beat is titled 'The Impossible Middle,' implying unresolved tension/standoff, but this line resolves the standoff preemptively via omniscient certainty, undercutting the impossibility.
findings.Fix: Soften to a guess/hope rather than certain knowledge: 'Tavi thought — hoped — Reza was about to let him through.'

findings.Quote: Looking would have made it a trade, and this wasn't a trade.
findings.Note: explanatory aphorism tells the reader the meaning of the gesture instead of trusting the physical action already shown
findings.Fix: cut the explanatory sentence and let the walking-past-without-looking carry the meaning unstated

findings.Quote: A pressure change, the kind that comes ahead of rain, rippling through the Volume around him.
findings.Note: weather metaphor undercuts the tech-thriller tension of a data leak going public; feels ornamental rather than diagnostic of the actual mechanism
findings.Fix: ground the sensation in the Volume's own physics/tech rather than a rain simile

findings.Quote: six-foot-three of paid-for muscle with nowhere to stand
findings.Note: cute noir-tough-guy self-description that undercuts the scene's flatness with a wink of style
findings.Fix: six-foot-three, and none of it useful now

findings.Quote: the word together had felt like a wall you could lean on instead of a door that opened onto nothing
findings.Note: Purple double-metaphor that strains under scrutiny — a wall and a door are contradictory vehicles for the same abstract idea, muddying rather than clarifying the betrayal.
findings.Fix: Pick one image: e.g. 'the word together had felt solid, not like the drop it turned out to be.'

findings.Quote: Ozzie hadn't slept. So Ozzie already knew. By now everybody did.
findings.Note: telling-not-showing chain of inference stacked as flat declarative fragments; asserts knowledge without evidence shown, undercutting the beat's momentum
findings.Fix: cut to one line or ground it in an observed detail, e.g. 'Ozzie's shape moved behind the glass, too fast for this hour.'

findings.Quote: a menu in four languages nobody in the room spoke
findings.Note: Cute-clever filler detail meant to signal atmosphere/irony but reads as an aphoristic aside rather than earned observation; slightly undercuts the tension of the meeting setup.
findings.Fix: Cut or replace with a concrete sensory detail that serves tension, e.g. 'a menu that hadn't changed in a decade.'

findings.Quote: Ordering left a record.
findings.Note: Functions as a flat expository aphorism explaining tradecraft logic rather than dramatizing his wariness; borderline telling-not-showing.
findings.Fix: Show the avoidance physically: 'He waved off the server twice.'

findings.Quote: that told him the money behind this was old and careful, patient enough to build a chain that long
findings.Note: Interpretive telling injected mid-dialogue beat; states the deduction outright instead of letting the terse dialogue and details imply it.
findings.Fix: Trim to the bare inference or cut, letting the cutout detail speak for itself.

findings.Quote: He was very good alone. He'd made himself that way on purpose.
findings.Note: Telling-not-showing; flat statement of character that restates the prior lines without adding new information.
findings.Fix: Cut, or replace with a concrete behavioral detail that demonstrates the skill instead of asserting it.

findings.Quote: the way you push a coin into a slot
findings.Note: Simile is inert filler—doesn't sharpen the image or reveal character, just restates the mechanical action.
findings.Fix: Cut the simile or replace with a detail specific to Vane's manner.

findings.Quote: courier work — the kind that paid fast and burned you just as fast, the kind you took at nineteen because nobody told you the come-up had a ceiling until your head hit it
findings.Fix: tighten the parallel clauses; the doubled 'kind' construction plus the ceiling/head metaphor stacks slightly too neatly for the register elsewhere in the chapter

findings.Quote: He read it twice, waiting for the numbers to disagree with each other. They didn't.
findings.Fix: consider cutting the second sentence or making the beat's mechanics (payment auth, non-refusable clause) do the work instead of this small aphoristic flourish

findings.Quote: with a bad slug and no clean way to set it down
findings.Note: Vague noir-ish phrasing that gestures at meaning without delivering concrete image or stakes.
findings.Fix: Specify what the 'bad slug' situation actually was.

findings.Quote: the cluster believed it
findings.Note: Anthropomorphizing the camera as 'believing' is a soft, slightly cute personification that undercuts the technical precision of the rest of the passage.
findings.Fix: "and the cluster logged it clean" or similar non-anthropomorphic phrasing.

findings.Quote: and was doing it now for someone they badly did not want to lose
findings.Note: vague pseudo-insight tacked on without grounding; reads as filler foreshadowing rather than earned deduction
findings.Fix: cut or replace with a concrete observed detail that supports the claim

findings.Quote: not running any of the three exits he'd mapped on the way up
findings.Note: awkward phrasing — 'running an exit' is unclear as a physical action; borders on mechanics confusion with 'not reaching' and 'not stepping back'
findings.Fix: clarify: 'not breaking for any of the three exits he'd mapped on the way up'

findings.Quote: He kept his shoulder to the wall and did not go looking.
findings.Note: Slightly vague physical beat that leans on genre-standard tension pose without specific sensory grounding.
findings.Fix: Add a concrete detail, e.g., 'He kept his shoulder to the wall, breath shallow, and did not go looking.'

findings.Quote: felt the quiet come floor by floor
findings.Note: Personifying encroaching silence as a physical arrival is a familiar thriller cadence.
findings.Fix: Specify what he actually perceives (e.g., 'counted the silence rising floor by floor').

findings.Quote: That discipline had kept him whole in six buildings worse than this one.
findings.Note: Tells backstory/competence via summary rather than showing; reads as stock hardened-operative exposition.
findings.Fix: Cut or replace with a specific memory fragment instead of a tally.

findings.Quote: with the same password he'd used since Pilsen
findings.Note: Undercuts the established tradecraft (rotating key, no log, three years of care) by revealing sloppy, static password use — reads as an inserted quirky detail rather than earned characterization.
findings.Fix: Either cut the password detail or reconcile it with the rotating-key security ('the rotating key itself seeded from a phrase he'd used since Pilsen').

findings.Quote: Say the name and it became a problem he had to solve. Leave it unsaid and it stayed a door he had to hold.
findings.Note: Aphoristic parallel structure reads as a pseudo-profound rule stated for its own neatness rather than earned by the scene.
findings.Fix: Ground the avoidance in a concrete detail (what saying it would force him to do) rather than a maxim.

findings.Quote: It told him the one thing it could tell him.
findings.Note: Circular, empty phrasing that withholds information without adding tension.
findings.Fix: State or gesture at the actual content, even obliquely.

findings.Quote: the stillness of someone who's already counted the exits
findings.Note: Familiar genre shorthand for wary/competent characters, verges on stock phrasing.
findings.Fix: Replace with a more specific physical tell unique to this character.

findings.Quote: It came out quieter than he meant.
findings.Note: Standard telling-not-showing tag for suppressed emotion, adds little beyond noting volume.
findings.Fix: Cut the tag or replace with a physical detail (throat, breath) that shows rather than states the effect.

findings.Quote: Tavi had been doing this long enough to know a cage when it had good furniture in it.
findings.Note: Aphoristic summary line that tells the reader the conclusion rather than trusting the preceding concrete details to land it.
findings.Fix: Cut the sentence and let the itemized details (guards, watch, rig) stand alone.

findings.Quote: He was twenty
findings.Note: Beat 0 frames Rafi as 'the kid' and beat 1 explicitly parallels him to Tavi 'at nineteen'; introducing his exact age as twenty here reads as an inconsistency in how his age has been treated (young/kid vs. specific adult age) rather than a clarification.
findings.Fix: Either drop the specific age or establish it earlier so the 'kid' framing and comparison to nineteen don't feel at odds.

findings.Quote: It was the walk of a man deciding where not to be.
findings.Note: Vague aphoristic phrasing that sounds thematic but doesn't add concrete information.
findings.Fix: Specify what the deliberateness looked like — pace, pauses, gaze.

findings.Quote: Someone had spent four years teaching that out of him, and it hadn't been Tavi.
findings.Note: Slightly vague aphoristic phrasing that tells rather than shows who did the training or why it matters here; reads as a portentous aside rather than concrete information.
findings.Fix: Name or hint at the trainer/organization, or cut to keep the beat purely kinetic.

findings.Quote: A graze, not a hole. It burned like a hole.
findings.Note: The line leans on a neat rhetorical flip (hole/not-a-hole) that reads as a crafted quip rather than raw sensation, slightly undercutting the immediacy of the injury.
findings.Fix: Describe the burn directly without the hole/not-hole wordplay, e.g. 'A graze. It burned white down to the bone.'

findings.Quote: His hardware was built for close. His body had always been built for close.
findings.Note: Redundant repetition of 'built for close' without adding new information; reads as filler emphasis rather than escalation.
findings.Fix: His hardware was built for close range; so was he.

findings.Quote: He came back like a man who's practiced getting hit.
findings.Note: Tense shift to present ('who's') breaks the past-tense narration and reads as an authorial aside rather than embedded observation.
findings.Fix: He came back like a man who'd practiced getting hit.

findings.Quote: Staying meant finished.
findings.Note: Terse aphorism-style filler that tells rather than shows the stakes.
findings.Fix: Cut or replace with a concrete physical detail of why staying down would kill him.

findings.Quote: The job had its ending written in already.
findings.Note: Vague pseudo-fatalistic aphorism that doesn't earn its weight or connect concretely to action.
findings.Fix: Cut or ground it in a specific observed detail instead of abstract fatalism.

findings.Quote: his eyes went somewhere between forgiving and beaten and settled on neither
findings.Note: vague abstraction stands in for a concrete visual — tells an emotional state rather than showing it
findings.Fix: describe an actual physical detail (twitch, flick of gaze) instead of naming abstract emotional poles

findings.Quote: Held it. Held it.
findings.Note: repetition aims for tension but reads as filler padding rather than earned suspense
findings.Fix: cut one repetition or replace with a concrete beat (a breath, a tremor) to justify the pause

findings.Quote: taking the direction with nothing at the end of it
findings.Note: vague, portentous phrasing that tells rather than shows what Reza's departure means
findings.Fix: state plainly what lies that direction or cut the qualifier

findings.Quote: blood-sweet, thick enough to taste
findings.Note: stock sensory intensifier pattern for gore/smell
findings.Fix: find a more specific, less formulaic descriptor

findings.Quote: Someone had copied the slug before he ever carried it. They'd been waiting for a moment like this to let it loose.
findings.Note: asserts motive/plot mechanics as flat exposition, telling the reader the conspiracy's shape rather than letting Rafi piece it together
findings.Fix: filter through Rafi's inference so it reads as deduction, not omniscient narration

findings.Quote: like a man making sure it would stick
findings.Note: generic simile that doesn't add specific texture to Tavi's characterization
findings.Fix: replace with a concrete physical detail of how Tavi taught the route

findings.Quote: Rafi had kept it the way Gray Zone kids keep everything useful — without ceremony, without asking why.
findings.Note: aphoristic generalization about 'Gray Zone kids' that reads as authorial commentary rather than scene-grounded detail
findings.Fix: cut the sociological aside or replace with a specific memory beat

findings.Quote: unhurried and unsure, because the only other thing to do was stop
findings.Note: tips into aphorism-lite phrasing that tells us his state rather than showing it
findings.Fix: He started walking toward it, not sure why, just that stopping wasn't an option.

findings.Quote: a Gray Zone street the city had decided didn't exist
findings.Note: stock noir personification of a city 'deciding' a place is invisible
findings.Fix: a Gray Zone street with no listing, no patrol schedule, nothing

findings.Quote: He felt the altitude drain out of him. Slow and complete.
findings.Note: vague physical-metaphor-for-emotion shorthand, sentence fragment adds false weight
findings.Fix: He felt it go — the climb, the plan, all of it — slow and complete.

findings.Quote: believed — briefly, completely — that he was the kind of person that kitchen was built for
findings.Note: reads as a summarized-emotion aphorism rather than a specific image or beat
findings.Fix: had let himself think, for exactly as long as the coffee was hot, that the kitchen was his too

findings.Quote: The Φ0.40 lodged somewhere he'd feel later.
findings.Note: Vague deferred-feeling gesture that tells rather than shows, and the mechanics of where/how it 'lodges' are fuzzy filler.
findings.Fix: Cut the sentence or replace with a concrete physical/financial detail.

findings.Quote: Running was a confession, and he hadn't decided yet what he was confessing to.
findings.Note: Aphoristic quip that reads as authorial cleverness rather than character interiority.
findings.Fix: Cut or ground it in a concrete physical choice instead of a maxim.

findings.Quote: six-foot-three of it, all that corporate chrome catching no light
findings.Note: Contradictory sensory image — chrome that catches no light undercuts the visual specificity it's reaching for.
findings.Fix: Either commit to chrome catching dull light, or drop 'catching no light.'

findings.Quote: His jaw moved once, a small shift.
findings.Note: Slightly redundant phrasing (moved once/small shift say the same thing twice) reads as filler mechanics.
findings.Fix: Cut to 'His jaw moved once.'

findings.Quote: Reza picked up Tavi's cup, looked at it, set it back down without drinking. Tavi let him.
findings.Note: 'Tavi let him' tells us permission/tolerance rather than showing any reaction, a slight telling-not-showing beat.
findings.Fix: Cut the line or replace with a concrete physical beat from Tavi.

findings.Quote: "You knew I'd take it if you handed it off?"
findings.Note: The referent of 'it' is ambiguous — could be the egress or something else — muddying what should be a sharp confrontation beat.
findings.Fix: Specify: 'You knew I'd take the egress if you handed it off?'

findings.Quote: the ceramic level with the air now, past any pretending
findings.Note: vague, purple phrasing that doesn't clarify what physical or emotional state it's describing — reads as reaching for profundity without content
findings.Fix: cut 'past any pretending' or replace with a concrete detail

findings.Quote: the way you take a thing you've decided to believe in
findings.Note: stock sentimental-simile construction ('the way you...') that tells us the emotional resonance rather than showing it
findings.Fix: replace with a concrete physical detail of the kid's grip or face
